# collapse_ints

collapse_ints(nums) sorts the distinct integers in nums and joins them with commas, writing every run of 4 OR MORE consecutive integers as first-last. Inside a range, a negative endpoint is written in parentheses; outside a range, numbers are written plainly. collapse_ints([]) == "".

Examples:

- `collapse_ints([13, -8, 0]) == '-8,0,13'`
- `collapse_ints([-5, 14, 8, -1, -8, -7, 11, -3, 5]) == '-8,-7,-5,-3,-1,5,8,11,14'`

from solution import collapse_ints
# sanity: ranges, negative endpoints, duplicates, empty
assert collapse_ints([]) == ""
assert collapse_ints([1,2,3,4]) == "1-4"
assert collapse_ints([-4,-3,-2,-1]) == "(-4)-(-1)"
assert collapse_ints([-2,-1,0,1]) == "(-2)-1"

assert collapse_ints([11,13,6,-2,12,1,0,-3]) == '-3,-2,0,1,6,11,12,13'
# purity: same input twice
x = [3,1,2,4,0]
assert collapse_ints(x) == collapse_ints(x)
print("all sanity checks passed")
EOF
